clue.text: Bitter moan about plant in garden

indicators.note: about here means turned around or moved about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone moans bitterly about a plant growing in their garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals the anagram of BITTER MOAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Montbretia is a hardy orange-flowered perennial grown in gardens, a crocosmia hybrid.

clue.text: Way holy person is unassuming

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy person

explanation.surface: The path followed by a holy person is a humble one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a person without pretension or self-importance is both unassuming and modest.

clue.text: Small numbers — in what way is that something bothering restaurant?

parts.note: NOS is the short form of numbers, so a small version of the word
how asks in what way

explanation.surface: A restaurant asks how small numbers of diners can be a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' shortens 'numbers' to its abbreviation NOS rather than describing the numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner who books a table and never turns up is a nuisance that costs a restaurant takings.

clue.text: Like a drippy type showing no interest whatever?

definitions.text: Like a drippy type showing no interest whatever?

parts.words: Like a drippy type showing no interest whatever?
parts.note: a drippy, weepy person is in tears; one completely uninterested is utterly weary, and the idiom for that extreme tedium mentions tears

explanation.surface: A description of a wet, feeble person who cares about nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for extreme boredom is read literally: the drippy type is brought to the point of crying.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means utterly wearied by tedium, and read literally it fits someone weepy.

clue.text: They hear corny things

definitions.meaning: the organs of hearing on either side of the head
the seed-bearing spikes of maize or wheat, things made of corn

explanation.surface: Organs of hearing that, in a silly world, pick up corny jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of hearing and the grain-bearing head of a cereal plant share one word.

clue.text: What may be played in tents that's naughty and full of spirit

indicators.note: full of means one piece is filled with another, which sits inside it
naughty means misbehaving, so the letters of the words in tents are put out of order

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Something naughty and boozy goes on in the tents at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges IN TENTS to INSTENT; 'full of' puts RUM inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical instrument is something that is played, like a violin or piano.

clue.text: Posed outside back of shop in row

indicators.note: outside means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a model sat or posed for a portrait

indicators.note: back of points to the final letter of the word shop

explanation.surface: Someone posed outside the rear of a shop during an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, and a row is a noisy argument, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Bad legislation? Such would supposedly help the needy

definitions.meaning: laws that are poor in quality, playfully read

definitions.text: Such would supposedly help the needy
definitions.meaning: historic English statutes for relief of paupers, laws for the poor

explanation.surface: A question about badly drafted laws meant to aid those in need.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic English statutes for relieving paupers, read also as laws of low quality.

clue.text: Attempt to get hold of liquid, out-of-this-world bathroom item

indicators.note: to get hold of means the first piece grips the others inside it

parts.note: to try is to attempt
oil is a liquid
ET, the extra-terrestrial, is literally out of this world

explanation.surface: An attempt to grab some alien liquid ends up in the bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Toiletries are soaps, creams and the like kept in a bathroom for washing and grooming.

clue.text: Abandon girl in shrub

parts.note: to desert is to abandon
Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Leave a girl alone among the bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrub' hides the flower in ROSE, but here Rose is just a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenium, a succulent flowering shrub of arid regions, is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: American native given greeting outside work

indicators.note: outside means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A Native American is greeted outside his place of work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Native American people of north-eastern Arizona.

clue.text: Naval officers raised alarm at sea after first sign of rocks

indicators.note: after means the rearranged words follow the single letter
first sign of points to the opening letter of the word rocks
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Sailors raise the alarm on spotting rocks at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks part of the naval picture but signals the anagram of RAISED ALARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear admiral is a senior naval rank, just below vice admiral.

clue.text: In middle of lesson get unfriendly rebukes

indicators.note: In means the second piece goes inside the first
middle of points to the two central letters of the word lesson

parts.note: someone cold is distant and unfriendly

explanation.surface: A teacher turns unfriendly midway through a lesson and tells pupils off.
explanation.walkthrough: With an even number of letters, a word's middle is two letters, not one.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold someone is to rebuke them, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Awful trouble with EU showing no love for diehard Tory?

indicators.note: awful means terrible, so the letters are mangled into a new order
showing no means the following letter is dropped from the word trouble

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A staunch Conservative finds dreadful trouble with the EU and no affection for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing no' removes O from TROUBLE, leaving TRUBLE; 'Awful' rearranges that with EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is the Conservative colour, so a staunchly loyal Tory is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Attacked dwelling and was effective

parts.note: struck means hit or attacked
a home is a dwelling

explanation.surface: Raiders attacked a house and their assault worked.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a remark or blow that hits its target has had the intended impact.

clue.text: Special collection of least well-regarded artist?

definitions.meaning: household linen and goods gathered by a bride-to-be for married life
a painter at the very bottom of the rankings, a drawer being someone who draws

explanation.surface: A gallery's special collection is made up of works by its worst-rated painter.
explanation.walkthrough: A drawer is also one who draws; 'bottom drawer' is the British term for a hope chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The British name for a trousseau kept by a woman preparing to marry, and literally the lowest-ranked sketcher.

clue.text: Quickly providing two portions of meat

indicators.note: two means the piece is used twice in a row

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat, such as lamb or pork

explanation.surface: A butcher quickly serves up a pair of meat cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal exclamation means hurry up or be quick about it.

clue.text: A passionate knight going out is fragrant

indicators.note: going out means the following letter leaves the word before it

parts.note: romantic means amorous or passionate
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An ardent knight heads out smelling sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the knight in chess notation, since K is taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something with a pleasant, spicy scent is both aromatic and fragrant.

clue.text: Buffoonery of liar had Queen troubled

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A lying courtier's antics upset the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A harlequinade is a slapstick pantomime featuring Harlequin, hence clowning or buffoonery.

clue.text: Conflict? It's upset ref badly

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A footballer complains that the referee is unsettled by a bad decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the letters of IT'S REF; 'badly' backs it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: strife is bitter disagreement or conflict.

clue.text: Traditional manufacturer needs entitlement to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard means the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: a right is an entitlement

explanation.surface: A long-established manufacturer insists on being heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A wright is an old word for a maker or builder, as in shipwright or wheelwright.

clue.text: Exercises to get bit of money by bankrupt college

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: bit of points to the first letter of the word money

parts.note: broke means out of money, bankrupt

explanation.surface: A cash-strapped college is reduced to selling exercise classes for a little money.
explanation.definitionFit: Pembroke is a college at both Oxford and Cambridge universities.

clue.text: German fellow's regimen accepted with bit of hesitation

parts.note: a diet is a regimen of eating
er is the sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: A German man's eating plan is taken up somewhat reluctantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German fellow's' looks possessive, but the 's is simply 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieter is a common German male name.

clue.text: Stars in disgrace sometimes

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of the following two words

explanation.surface: Celebrities sometimes fall into disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is an expert or star performer, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Emotion created by speed getting heart going

indicators.note: getting heart going means the central letter is removed

parts.note: haste is speed

explanation.surface: A racing pulse stirs up strong feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting heart going' removes the middle letter S from HASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate, an intense dislike, is one of the strong emotions.

clue.text: Prisoner on top level said to be hiding away

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: said to be means the word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: the ceiling is the top level of a room, or an upper limit

explanation.surface: A convict on the top floor is reportedly lying low.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealing means keeping hidden away from view.

clue.text: Gait of the old man going to church

parts.note: pa is father, informally the old man
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Dad's walk on the way to church.
explanation.definitionFit: Pace is a manner of walking, which is what gait means.

clue.text: Determined little girl, ten, saucy on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means the first piece wraps around the others

parts.note: pert means cheeky or saucy
sis is short for sister, a little girl
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky ten-year-old girl who won't give up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone persistent keeps going firmly, which is being determined.
